s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Food security is necessary even in surplus food production years.
Reason (R) : Starvation can still occur due to unequal distribution and lack of accessibility.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
x: Food security does not mean only production/availability; it also means physical and economic access for every person, at all times, to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food. Therefore, even if a year has surplus overall production, hunger and malnutrition may continue if distribution is unequal, transport/storage/logistics are weak, access to remote or disaster-affected areas is difficult, prices remain high, or purchasing power is low. Hence, Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is also true, and (R) correctly explains (A).

s:
With reference to 'ANNA DARPAN' project consider the following statements.
A. It is initiated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare Government of India.
B. Its objective is to modernise the Supply Chain Management System.
C. It is also known as 'Depot Online system'.
D. It will not cover its operations at Mandis, Mills and Depots (both owned and hired) as well as divisional, regional, zonal and headquarters levels.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Food Corporation of India (FCI), under the Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India has embarked on a comprehensive digital transformation initiative in 2024 to modernize its existing supply chain management system, known as the 'Depot Online System'. This ambitious project involves the implementation of a new, microservices-based integrated supply chain management system named 'ANNA DARPAN'. The system is being designed to streamline and enhance the entire supply chain operations and services at various levels including Mandis, Mills, Depots (both owned and hired), as well as divisional, regional, zonal, and headquarters operations. This transformation is supported by advanced technology, a stateof-the-art IT environment , and an optimized architectural framework. To bring this vision to life, FCI has engaged M/s Coforge Limited as the system integrator (SI). This selection was finalized with the signing of the contract on 14th June, 2024. M/s Coforge Limited shall be responsible for the end-to-end design, development, implementation, and maintenance of the ANNA DARPAN system. Hence, statements of option (b) and (c) are correct while statements of option (a) and (d) are incorrect.

s: Under which law, the State Food Commission is established?
x: Section 16 of the National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA), notified on 10.09.2013 provides that every State Government shall, by notification, constitute a State Food Commission for the purpose of monitoring and review of implementation of this Act. The State Food Commission shall consist of a Chairperson, five other Members and a Member-Secretary with associated administrative and technical staff. Section 19 provides that two or more States may have a joint State Food Commission with the approval of the Central Government.

With reference to the National Food Security Act, which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. It will cover upto 75 percent rural and 50 percent urban population.
II. Special focus on nutritional support to women and children.
III. Eldest woman of above 18 years age will be head of household.

o: I, II and III are correct
x: The enactment of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 on July 5, 2013 marks a paradigm shift in the approach to food security from welfare to rights based approach. This Act was notified on September 10, 2013 and came into force with retrospective effect from July 5, 2013. Major provisions of NFSA, 2013 are : O The Act legally entitles upto 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population to receive subsidised foodgrains under Targeted Public Distribution System, thus covering about two-thirds of the population. O The eligible households will be entitled to receive 5 kg foodgrains per person per month at Rs. 3,2,1 per kg for rice, wheat and coarse grains, respectively. O The existing Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households (i.e. poorest of the poor) will continue to receive 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month. O The eldest woman in the household, 18 years or above, shall be head of the household for the issuance of the ration card. O The Act also has a special focus on the nutritional support to women and children.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding "National Food Security Act" (NFSA) in India :
A. It was enacted on July 5, 2013.
B. Around 50 crore persons have been covered under NFSA at present.
C. The Act legally entitles upto 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population to receive subsidized foodgrains.
Choose the correct option using codes :
o: Both B and C are correct
Both A and B are correct
Both A and C are correct
A, B and C are correct
x: National Food Security Act (NFSA) was signed into law on 10 September, 2013, retroactive to 5 July, 2013. The enactment of the NFSA, 2013 on 5 July, 2013 (Originally as an Ordinance) marks a paradigm shift in the approach to food security from welfare to rights based approach. The Act legally entitles upto 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population to receive subsidized foodgrains under Targeted Public Distribution System. About two thirds of the population therefore is covered under the Act to receive highly subsidized foodgrains. The Act is being implemented in all the States/UTs, and on all India basis, out of maximum coverage of 81.34 crore persons, around 80 crore persons have been covered under NFSA at present. Hence, statement A and C are correct, while statement B is incorrect.

s: What is the objective of Community Development Programmes?
x: The community development programme was started in India, just after independence (in October, 1952). It was a multi-project programme with the aim of an overall development of rural people. In 1957, Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended for ‘Democratic Decentralization’. After Independence, the first organized attempt to develop village cattle on an effective scale was initiated with the launch of Key Village Scheme (KVS) in August,1952. KVS was a general comprehensive scheme drawn up by Government of India for development of cattle population in India by employing scientific methods for improvement of cattle. The Central Government established District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) in 1980 as a body of professionals to plan, monitor and evaluate rural development programmes at district level. DRDA Administration Scheme was introduced from 1st April, 1999. The DRDA is the principal organ at the district level to manage and oversee the implementation of different anti-poverty programmes of the Ministry of Rural Development.

The National Committee on the Development of Backwards Areas reviewed the performance of this programme. Pair 2 is incorrect: The Desert Development Programme (DDP) by the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, aims to minimise the adverse effects of drought and control desertification by rejuvenating the natural resource base of identified desert areas. s: Rural Sanitation Strategy launched by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in September 2019 relates to which of the following periods?
x: The Ministry of Jal Shakti has launched the 10-year Rural Sanitation Strategy starting from 2019 up to 2029. The strategy has been prepared by DDWS (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation) in consultation with the State Governments and other stakeholders. The strategy aims to sustain the aims of the Swachh Bharat Mission- Grameen, ensuring sustained access to safely managed sanitation for all rural Indians and achieving a clean living environment through solid and liquid waste management.

s: Jal Jeevan Mission Scheme was declared in the Union Budget of which Financial Year?
x: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), a Central Government initiative under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, aims to ensure access of piped water to every household in India. The mission’s goal was to provide all households in rural India safe and adequate water through individual household tap connections by 2024. This mission was launched by the PM Narendra Modi on 15 August, 2019 from the ramparts of Red Fort. The ‘Har Ghar Nal Se Jal’ programme was announced by the Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in her Budget 2019-20 Speech. This programme forms a crucial part of the Jal Jeevan Mission. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. Union Budget 2025- 26 has extended the Jal Jeevan Mission till 2028 with the aim of benefitting the remaining (about 20%) rural households. Rural households with tap water connection at the launch of JJM (i.e., as on 15 August, 2019) were around 3.24 crore only (16.72% of total rural households). As on 29 May, 2026, under JJM (since its inception) around 12.62 crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 29 May, 2026, out of about 19.36 crore rural households in the country, about 15.86 crore (81.91%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes.

s: Which programme was approved by the Union Cabinet in April, 2025 to develop border villages ?
x: In April 2025, the Union Cabinet approved the Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II) for the comprehensive development of border villages and for improving their living standards. This programme focuses on the socioeconomic development of villages located in blocks abutting international land borders, strengthening basic infrastructure and amenities, and expanding livelihood opportunities, with the objective of developing border villages.

x: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojna (PMGSY) was started on 25 December, 2000. The objective of the PMGSY is to provide all-weather road connectivity, to the eligible unconnected habitations in the rural areas with a population of 500 persons and above in plain areas. In respect of hill States, the desert areas and the tribal areas, the objective would be to connect eligible unconnected habitations with a population of 250 persons and above. In this scheme the rural roads to be taken up will, by and large, be surface roads (black topped/cement concrete). However, depending upon the soil conditions, all-weather roads may also be gravel roads, but with all necessary cross-drainage structures.

s: PURA (Providing Urban Amenities to Rural Areas) model was advocated by :
x: Providing Urban Amenities to Rural Areas (PURA) is a strategy for rural development in India. This concept was given by the former President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. x: There is sufficient evidence to suggest that MGNREGA has contributed to : (i) increased rural wages everywhere and substantial increase in purchasing power of rural poor; (ii) reduced distress migration from traditionally migration-intensive areas; (iii) usage of barren areas for cultivation; and (iv) empowerment of the weaker sections and giving them a new sense of identity and bargaining power.

s: Which of the following is a cause of rural to urban migration in India?
x: No single factor causes rural-to-urban migration in India; instead, it is a combination of 'push' factors, like rural poverty, lack of employment (few jobs in rural areas), and inadequate basic services, and 'pull' factors, such as urban job opportunities (high labour demand in cities), better living standards, education, and infrastructure, that drive people to cities. While the desire for a better life and economic stability is a primary motivator, the decision to migrate is influenced by a complex interplay of economic, social, and environmental conditions (including unbalanced rural-urban development) in both rural and urban areas. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.
